qt: to the Commission Loránt Vincze (PPE), Hannes Heide (S&D), Raquel García Hermida-Van Der Walle (Renew), Oihane Agirregoitia Martínez (Renew), Annamária Vicsek (PfE), Kinga Gál (PfE), Viktória Ferenc (PfE), Waldemar Tomaszewski (ECR), Gabriella Gerzsenyi (PPE), Zoltán Tarr (PPE), Kinga Kollár (PPE), Dóra Dávid (PPE), András Tivadar Kulja (PPE) Subject:

As Members of the European Parliament, we express serious concern regarding recent amendments to the Slovak Criminal Code which introduce criminal liability, including up to six months of imprisonment, for questioning the so-called Beneš decrees. These decrees include ordinances that enabled the confiscation of immovable property on the grounds of belonging to a national minority. While the Commission has previously characterised the decrees as historical acts, information reported by the Slovak Land Fund indicates that, in recent years, hundreds of individuals, including citizens of other EU Member States, have had land confiscated without compensation under this legal framework. This indicates that these decrees continue to produce legal effects. Such practices raise serious concerns as regards compliance with EU law. 1.
How does the Commission assess the compatibility of these national practices with the rule of law, including the continued legal effects of the decrees on property rights?
What is the Commission’s assessment of legal provisions introducing criminal liability for public or academic discussion of the decrees, in the light of freedom of expression?
How will the Commission ensure that EU funds are not used to support discriminatory practices and that the free movement of capital is fully upheld?
at: (English version) to the Commission Loránt Vincze (PPE), Hannes Heide (S&D), Raquel García Hermida-Van Der Walle (Renew), Oihane Agirregoitia Martínez (Renew), Annamária Vicsek (PfE), Kinga Gál (PfE), Viktória Ferenc (PfE), Waldemar Tomaszewski (ECR), Gabriella Gerzsenyi (PPE), Zoltán Tarr (PPE), Kinga Kollár (PPE), Dóra Dávid (PPE), András Tivadar Kulja (PPE) (22 December 2025) Subject: Serious concerns regarding compliance with European values and EU law in Slovakia As Members of the European Parliament, we express serious concern regarding recent amendments to the Slovak Criminal Code which introduce criminal liability, including up to six months of imprisonment, for questioning the so-called Beneš decrees. These decrees include ordinances that enabled the confiscation of immovable property on the grounds of belonging to a national minority. While the Commission has previously characterised the decrees as historical acts, information reported by the Slovak Land Fund indicates that, in recent years, hundreds of individuals, including citizens of other EU Member States, have had land confiscated without compensation under this legal framework. This indicates that these decrees continue to produce legal effects. Such practices raise serious concerns as regards compliance with EU law. 1. How does the Commission assess the compatibility of these national practices with the rule of law, including the continued legal effects of the decrees on property rights? 2. What is the Commission’s assessment of legal provisions introducing criminal liability for public or academic discussion of the decrees, in the light of freedom of expression? 3. How will the Commission ensure that EU funds are not used to support discriminatory practices and that the free movement of capital is fully upheld? (21 April 2026) The Commission is committed, within the remit of its competences, to ensure that fundamental freedoms, such as the free movement of capital, and fundamental rights, as established under the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union (1), including the right to freedom of expression, the right to property and the right to non-discrimination, are upheld. In accordance with Article 51(1) of the Charter, its provisions only apply to Member States when they implement EU law. The Commission is aware of the recent adopted law criminalising the questioning of the ‘Beneš decrees’. The Commission is closely monitoring the matter and assessing the information available. As regards disbursement of EU funds, the effective implementation of the Charter is crucial for EU-funded projects under the Common Provisions Regulation, where Member States must ensure the fulfilment of the enabling Charter condition throughout the programming period. In Slovakia, all calls for proposals are reviewed by the Ministry of Labour, Social Affairs and Family to ensure alignment with the Charter before approval (2). The Monitoring Committee, including Member State authorities, civil society representatives, and the Commission, assesses the fulfilment of the Charter enabling condition throughout the programming period.
